topPRs.title: compliance: spec improvements from fma
topPRs.author: 0xOneTony
topPRs.body:
Spec fixes from the bridge hook FMA review, on top of #971, grouped by failure mode.

**FM2: Completions publish more deposit gas than one L2 block can take**
- The published deposit gas count covers the whole L1 block in which a hook is set or removed.

**FM3: A withdrawal calls the hook or the bridge's escrow functions**
- `completeWithdrawalTransaction` reverts if the target is an Unsafe Target at the time of completion.

**FM9: The policy screens the wrong parties**
- The policy always receives two parties, sender then recipient, decoded only from messages the messengers sent.
- The module reads the L1 bridge and messenger addresses from the Portal's `SystemConfig` when deployed.
- New `parties()` view returns the same two addresses.

**FM10: A clearance outlives the check it was written for**
- Completion passes the policy the record's `clearedAt`.

**FM12 / FM17: A compromised policy / a wrong disable cutoff**
- `setPolicy`, `disable` and `enable` emit `PolicySet`, `Disabled` (with the cutoff) and `Enabled`.

**FM13: The module's balance stops covering what it holds**
- The bridge moves held tokens before the hook records the hold.

**FM15: Non-standard tokens break holds or completions**
- The module supports ETH, Native L1 Tokens and `OptimismMintableERC20` tokens.

**FM19: The hook stands between governance and L2**
- `depositTransaction` skips the hook for deposits sent by the ProxyAdmin owner, so governance actions on L2 never wait on screening. The overview's goals note the exception.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism-private/issues/823

topPRs.title: lagoon: specify that the block gas limit bounds pre-refund gas under SDM
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
SDM implementations already enforce the block gas limit against pre-refund gas, but the Lagoon specs never state it. This PR writes the rule down.

The rule is consensus-relevant. A client built from the spec could reasonably check the limit against canonical (post-refund) gas, which would admit more execution per block than op-reth and Kona accept, and the chain would split.

## Change

`sdm.md` gets a new **Block Gas Limit** subsection under Canonical Gas. Before executing transaction `i`, a verifier MUST check

```text
gasLimit(i) <= blockGasLimit - sum(evmGasUsed(j) for j < i)
```

A transaction that fails the check invalidates the block. This implies the usual check against canonical `gasUsed`, and is identical to it when a block carries no refunds.

It also adds a matching **Block resource limit** entry to Security Considerations. The entry notes that the EIP-7623 floor's resource bound survives SDM, because the floor is part of `evmGasUsed`.

## Implementation reference

`OpBlockExecutor::execute_transaction_without_commit` in [`rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/mod.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/ca63e7ee6fbb23b4f8b6ef97e7a5921e2ec4346a/rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/mod.rs#L1039-L1047) does the check by passing `blockGasLimit - evm_gas_used` to `validate_block_gas`. op-reth and the Kona executor share this code.

Found during the SDM FMA finalization review (FM3).

topPRs.title: rollup-node: Specify current_l1 invariants
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Specifies the guarantees that the `current_l1` field of `optimism_syncStatus` provides. The node must have fully processed all L1 blocks up to and including the parent of `current_l1`. It may include only part of the effects of `current_l1` itself. A reported value may be too low if it advances within a reasonable time, but it must never be too high.

The batcher, proposer and challenger depend on these guarantees. Until now the spec did not state them, so implementations such as kona-node could diverge from op-node.

Also corrects the `current_l1` description for the super root RPC. It required full processing of `current_l1`, but implementations now only guarantee full processing up to the parent block.

topPRs.title: deposits: Add invariants
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Adds an "Invariants" section to `deposits.md` stating the invariants the deposit rules follow:

1. A deposit transaction must always be valid to include in a block.
2. Deposits buy their gas on L1.
3. A deposit always mints on L2 exactly the amount of ETH deposited on L1.
4. The `sourceHash` of a deposit must be unique, so it must include all identifying components of the deposit.

Plus the cross-component invariant that the gas a deposit consumes is accounted for identically across the execution output and the block gas pool.

These are the positive invariants the current spec only states as a scattered set of "No X" negatives. Invariant 3 combines the two ETH-conservation directions: no ETH is created beyond the deposit, and no deposited ETH is lost.

topPRs.title: stage-1,deputy-pause-module: name the Foundation Upgrade Safe as the DeputyPauseModule foundation safe
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
The Stage 1 diagram and the DeputyPauseModule spec name the Foundation Operations Safe (`0x9BA6e03D8B90dE867373Db8cF1A58d2F7F006b3A`) as the Safe that controls the DeputyPauseModule. The live module is configured with the Foundation Upgrade Safe, and it is installed on the Security Council Guardian Safe. The DeputyPauseModule spec's own Overview already says the module is installed on the Guardian Safe.

On-chain evidence (Ethereum mainnet block 26245754):

```
cast call 0x09f7150D8c019BeF34450d6920f6B3608ceFdAf2 'getModulesPaginated(address,uint256)(address[],address)' 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001 10
# [0x76fC2F971FB355D0453cF9F64d3F9E4f640E1754]
cast call 0x76fC2F971FB355D0453cF9F64d3F9E4f640E1754 'foundationSafe()(address)'
# 0x847B5c174615B1B7fDF770882256e2D3E95b9D92   (Foundation Upgrade Safe)
cast call 0x76fC2F971FB355D0453cF9F64d3F9E4f640E1754 'guardianSafe()(address)'
# 0x09f7150D8c019BeF34450d6920f6B3608ceFdAf2   (Guardian Safe)
```

Changes:

- `stage-1.md`: the `pause` edge to the DeputyPauseModule now starts at the Foundation Upgrade Safe node that the diagram already has.
- `deputy-pause-module.md`: "Operations Safe" becomes "Foundation Safe", which matches the `foundationSafe` getter and the existing iDPM-005 and `setDeputy` text. Where the text names the Safe the module runs in, it now says the Security Council Guardian Safe.

`configurability.md` is not changed.

Reviewed with Codex (gpt-6-astra, high): no findings.
